qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Orthopedic surgeons face high switching costs due to familiarity with proprietary instrumentation, kinematics, and ROSA surgical robotics. However, structural pricing power is absent: hospital GPOs, Medicare DRG bundles, and international tenders (China VBP) inflict chronic -1% to -2% annual net price deflation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & negative pricing power, REJECT). While knee and hip implants benefit from surgeon switching costs, Zimmer Biomet structurally lacks pricing power, enduring -1% to -2% annual realized price deflation from hospital GPOs and government tenders (China VBP). 10-year median ROIC of ~7.5% falls well below the 12% Munger compounder threshold due to goodwill bloat from the Biomet merger and subsequent M&A.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is ~7.5% (FY23 4.5%, FY24 4.4%, FY25 ~3.5%), far below the 12% hurdle. High gross margins (69-71%) are offset by SG&A/R&D and amortization of intangibles. The 2015 Biomet merger saddled the balance sheet with over $8B in goodwill and intangibles. Net realized pricing is consistently negative (-1% to -2% per year) across reconstructive hips and knees, offsetting procedure volume gains. Total debt stands at ~$7.5B ($6.9B long-term), while competitive pressure from Stryker's Mako robotics platform continues to challenge ROSA.
